title: Silver Diamine Fluoride for Caries in Primary Teeth in Routine Clinical Practice
official: Efficacy and Safety of Silver Diamine Fluoride in Clinical Practice for the Treatment of Caries in Children With Primary Dentition
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how well and how safely silver diamine fluoride (SDF) stops tooth decay (caries) in baby teeth when it is used in routine dental care. It will include children aged 14 years or younger with caries in their primary (baby) teeth who are treated with SDF at a public primary care dental clinic. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What proportion of caries lesions treated with SDF do not progress after 12 months?
* How often do side effects occur, such as black staining of the tooth, sensitivity, abscesses, gum or skin irritation, or allergy?
* How satisfied are parents with the treatment? Participants will receive SDF as part of their usual dental care and will attend check-up visits 1, 6, and 12 months after treatment, where the dentist will examine the treated teeth, assess oral hygiene, and ask about diet and any side effects. Parents will answer a short satisfaction questionnaire.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Boys and girls aged 14 years or younger
* Caries in primary teeth with an indication for SDF treatment according to section 4 of the Catalan Health Department guideline "Implementation of silver diamine fluoride treatment in primary and community care dental clinics: rationale and protocol for use"
* Signed informed consent from the parent or legal representative
* For participants aged 12 years or older, signed informed assent adapted to their level of understanding, in addition to the consent of their legal representatives

Exclusion Criteria:

* Spontaneous or provoked pain associated with the caries lesion
* Deep caries lesion close to the dental pulp, according to the investigator's judgment
* Objection by the parents or the child to the black staining caused by SDF
* Irreversible pulpitis or pulp necrosis
* Active oral ulcers or gingivostomatitis
* History of allergy to silver, ammonia, or iodine
* Participation in another study involving an experimental intervention during the period of this study and/or with a visit schedule incompatible with this study
